findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting.
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11(P) Person In Charge. The PERSON IN CHARGE shall ensure that: (P) FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with LAW, to the PERSON IN CHARGE, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD, as specified under 2-201.11(A).

On arrival the PIC was unable to provide verification that the food handlers were notified and acknowledge their responsibility to report potential foodborne illness related symptoms and diagnosis. A fresh copy of the Reporting Agreement given out by SCDPH was given to the PIC. They are instructed to make copies and have all food handlers in the facility review and sign one. Maintain these copies available at the facility for future verifications. The inspector planned to follow-up on this matter at the same time that the sink repairs were reviewed 10 days from this inspection.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. 

On arrival there was not an available procedure for cleaning up vomit/diarrheal events in the facility. A fresh copy of the procedure given by SCDPH was given during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that a procedure is maintained at the facility and that all staff know where it is and how to use it moving forward.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands. 

1) An employee was observed to don gloves without hand washing. 2) An employee was observed to begin handling food contact single service items without hand washing. Education was conducted and the PIC was instructed to review hand washing, specifically WHEN to wash hands with all staff in the facility. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times required by the code moving forward.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

Raw eggs were observed over milk in the display walk in cooler. The PIC was consulted and the eggs moved to the bottom shelf to correct. Ensure that foods in the coolers are stored so that raw items are not stored over items that are considered Ready-To-Eat.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the sanitizer available in the three part sink was observed low on the inspector’s test strips. Approximate concentration of quat was observed below 100 ppm. This chemical needs a minimum concentration of 200-400 ppm to effectively sanitizer food contact surfaces. The kitchen staff and PIC were consulted and remade the water to correct. Only a single table was placed in the sink at that time and was not sufficient for reaching the correct concentration. Education was conducted and the bottle read to them. One tablet is sufficient for 1.5 gallons of water and there were 3-4 gallons of water in the sink at the time that it was made. More tablets were added to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are produced and maintained at effective concentrations at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

1) Paper boats were observed with the food contact surfaces up/exposed behind the hot holding/display area. The PIC was shown and the situation discussed The boats were flipped over to correct. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are protected from contamination via drifting or spraying contaminants at all times in the facility. 2) Boxes of styrofoam cups in the dry storage room were observed on the floor. The situation was discussed and the PIC is instructed to ensure that the food contact items are stored off the floor moving forward.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.citation_text:
5-402.13 Conveying Sewage. SEWAGE shall be conveyed to the point of disposal through an APPROVED sanitary SEWAGE system or other system, including use of SEWAGE transport vehicles, waste retention tanks, pumps, pipes, hoses, and connections that are constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

1) The three part sink cannot be drained without overflowing the pipe gap prior to entering the grease trap. 2) There appeared to be a break/crack in the pipe junction coming from the right sink of the three part sink. The PIC was instructed to acquire the use of a licensed plumber to consult and adjust the first item and repair/replace the second item. A follow up is being scheduled for ten days to allow time for maintenance to be conducted. Per the food program head an invoice will also be required to verify that the repair is conducted by a licensed plumber.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
(REPEAT from the pre-openings) 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

The following items continue to need maintenance from the pre-opening: 1) replace the acoustic ceiling tiles over the service counter and hot holding with smooth and easily cleanable variants; 2) patch the walls to the right of the three compartment sink. These locations were reviewed with the PIC and they are instructed to repair/replace prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

The mop was observed stored in dirty mop water in the mop bucket during this inspection. The situation was discussed and the PIC instructed to store the mop in such a way that it drip drys moving forward.
